title: Transfer of Northloop Protect Plans to the Recipient of a Gift
content:
**Clause.** A plan under the Northloop Protect Plans may be transferred, when the plan is transferable on gift, only to the recipient of an order marked as a gift; the coverage period and the claims already paid carry over unchanged.

All six plans are transferable on gift.

## The clause in parts

- **Who may receive the plan:** only the recipient of an order marked as a gift.
- **What changes:** the plan holder becomes the person the covered item was given to.
- **What does not change:** the coverage period (its coverage start and coverage end date) and the claims already paid on the plan.

## Basis questions answered

**Can a plan be moved to a family member when the covered order was not marked as a gift?**
No. A transfer is made only to the recipient of an order marked as a gift.

**Does the recipient receive a fresh coverage term?**
No. The coverage period carries over unchanged.

**Does the recipient start with the full limit again?**
No. The claims already paid carry over unchanged, so the settlements paid before the transfer remain counted against the plan.

## Hypothetical illustration

A covered order was marked as a gift, the covered item was delivered to the recipient on 2026-03-12, and the plan's coverage end date is 2028-03-11, with 200.00 USD of claims already paid. After the plan is transferred to the recipient, the recipient holds the plan, coverage still ends on 2028-03-11, and the claims paid still stand at 200.00 USD.
